taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-26, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 17.9 | 13.68 | 13.68
2 | 50.4 | 5.82 | 19.50
3 | 514.6 | 0.68 | 20.18
4 | 502.0 | 17.67 | 37.85
5 | 194.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AKQ-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-26, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station T-26, Survey Area T. The interpreted subsurface model for this station comprises five distinct layers. The resistivity profile shows an initial increase from 17.9 Ωm (Layer 1) to 514.6 Ωm (Layer 3), followed by a decrease through Layer 4 (502.0 Ωm) and Layer 5 (194.4 Ωm). Following the curve-type notation rules, the resistivity transitions for the three consecutive groups (1-2-3, 2-3-4, and 3-4-5) correspond to A, K, and Q respectively. Therefore, the calculated curve type is AKQ, which is consistent with the classification currently on file.

{"curve_type_stated": "AKQ", "label_issue_flagged": false}
